guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / asthma attack; BTS/SIGN Asthma guidelines
title: Asthma attack at a crowded music festival
setting: Music festival. An individual near an outdoor stage experiencing breathing difficulties. Distressed, gasping, only managing single words.
verdictExplanation: Severe respiratory distress (breathing rate 28/min, oxygen saturation 91%, gasping single-word speech). Sick: immediate reliever inhaler and 999 needed.

shared.danger: High number of bystanders around the patient
shared.airway: Breathing affected by asthma attack, audible wheeze

history.history: Triggered by dust and crowd at the main stage. Inhaler is in their bag.
history.drugs: Blue reliever (salbutamol) and brown preventer inhalers
history.additional: Expresses frustration about missing out on the festival activities

followUp.question: What is the correct immediate action for this severe asthma attack?

options.text: Sit them upright, help them take up to 10 puffs of their blue salbutamol inhaler via spacer, and call 999
Lay them flat on their back and encourage deep breaths into a paper bag
Administer their brown preventer inhaler as a first-line emergency medication
Do nothing; wait for them to calm down as it is likely a panic attack

followUp.explanation: Sit the patient upright to ease breathing. Help them take their blue reliever (salbutamol) inhaler (1 puff every 30-60 seconds up to 10 puffs). Call 999 immediately as they are in severe respiratory distress (SpO₂ 91%, gasping, only managing single words). Reliever is used, not preventer. Panic bags are dangerous in asthma.

evolvingStage.narrative: After taking 6 puffs of their blue inhaler and moving to a quiet area, their breathing eases significantly. The audible wheeze has reduced, and they can now speak in full sentences.

followUp.question: The patient's condition has improved. How does this alter your management plan?

options.text: Continue to monitor closely, allow them to rest, and liaise with ambulance control about downgrading or cancelling the response if fully recovered
Administer 10 more puffs of the inhaler immediately just to be safe, then discharge them
Tell them to return to the crowd immediately as they are no longer sick
Lay them flat to recover their energy for the rest of the festival

followUp.explanation: If the asthma attack resolves completely with treatment, they should be observed. You can discuss downgrading or cancelling the ambulance with control, but they still need rest and monitoring before returning to a dusty, crowded environment.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Reassure, sit upright. Assist with blue salbutamol inhaler. Call 999.
levelFlags.erNotes: Provide high-flow oxygen. Assist with salbutamol via spacer or nebulizer if available. Sit upright, monitor vital signs, prepare for emergency transfer.
